name: Mutual TLS
description: Require client certificates using mutual TLS (mTLS).

USE_MTLS.help: Enable client authentication with mutual TLS.
USE_MTLS.label: Use mutual TLS

MTLS_CA_CERTIFICATE_PRIORITY.help: Source of the client CA bundle: file path or base64/PEM data (file or data).
MTLS_CA_CERTIFICATE_PRIORITY.label: Client CA bundle priority

MTLS_CA_CERTIFICATE.help: Path to the trusted client CA bundle (PEM), readable by the Scheduler, which validates it, caches it, and distributes it to every instance (priority 'file'). Required when MTLS_VERIFY_CLIENT is set to on or optional.
MTLS_CA_CERTIFICATE.label: Client CA bundle

MTLS_CA_CERTIFICATE_DATA.help: Client CA bundle as base64 or plaintext PEM (priority 'data').
MTLS_CA_CERTIFICATE_DATA.label: Client CA bundle data (base64/plaintext)

MTLS_VERIFY_CLIENT.help: Client verification mode. 'on' requires a valid certificate on every HTTPS request. 'optional' asks for a certificate, refuses an invalid one and enforces nothing more unless MTLS_URL is set. 'optional_no_ca' asks for a certificate without validating it against a CA (diagnostics only, not real protection) and enforces nothing without MTLS_URL either. Plain HTTP follows MTLS_HTTP_POLICY.
MTLS_VERIFY_CLIENT.label: Verify client mode

MTLS_URL.help: Regex on the normalized request URI, case-sensitive ((?i) to ignore case), anchored on a directory: an index redirect skips a rule anchored on a file name. Requires a valid client certificate only on matching paths (HTTP only): set MTLS_VERIFY_CLIENT to optional. Runs before the whitelist (PLUGINS_ORDER_ACCESS). An invalid regex is reported at startup and fails closed. Several paths: MTLS_URL_1, MTLS_URL_2. Empty: no per-path rule (the whole site needs MTLS_VERIFY_CLIENT=on).
MTLS_URL.label: mTLS URL

MTLS_HTTP_POLICY.help: What to do with a plain HTTP request that mTLS should have protected: every path when MTLS_VERIFY_CLIENT is on, the MTLS_URL paths otherwise (nothing under optional or optional_no_ca without MTLS_URL). 'redirect' sends it to HTTPS (denied when there is no usable Host), 'deny' refuses it, 'allow' serves it as before for server-wide mode (MTLS_URL paths stay denied). An HTTPS redirect already issued by the SSL plugin comes first, and ACME HTTP-01 challenges that a solver owns are never touched.
MTLS_HTTP_POLICY.label: HTTP policy

MTLS_COUNT_BAD_BEHAVIOR.help: Let Bad Behavior count the failures mTLS itself causes: the 400 nginx answers when the client certificate is missing or invalid, and the mTLS denials (per-path rule, HTTP policy). When no, a client without a valid certificate is never banned for that alone; other 400 errors on the service still count.
MTLS_COUNT_BAD_BEHAVIOR.label: Count mTLS failures in Bad Behavior

MTLS_VERIFY_DEPTH.help: Maximum certificate chain depth accepted during client verification.
MTLS_VERIFY_DEPTH.label: Verify depth

MTLS_FORWARD_CLIENT_HEADERS.help: Forward verification results to upstream backends using X-SSL-Client-* headers. Client-supplied X-SSL-* headers are always stripped on ingress, so these values cannot be spoofed.
MTLS_FORWARD_CLIENT_HEADERS.label: Forward client headers

MTLS_CRL.help: Optional path to a certificate revocation list (PEM), readable by the Scheduler, which validates it, caches it, and distributes it to every instance (priority 'file'). nginx needs a CRL from every CA that issues a certificate of the chain, the root included, and refuses every client of a chain whose CRL is past its next update. A revoked certificate can keep resuming a TLS session saved before the CRL was published, for up to a day, until nginx is restarted. Leave empty to skip CRL checks.
MTLS_CRL.label: Client CRL path

MTLS_CRL_PRIORITY.help: Source of the CRL: file path or base64/PEM data (file or data).
MTLS_CRL_PRIORITY.label: Client CRL priority

MTLS_CRL_DATA.help: CRL as base64 or plaintext PEM (priority 'data').
MTLS_CRL_DATA.label: Client CRL data (base64/plaintext)
